head: d7ff72b0266c
answers: The reviewer's round-4 changes request at bc29f804: the important finding and all four minor ones. Four threads answered and resolved.

proof.criterion: The important finding: in the document-wide step any newline passed for a block edge, so a line inside another paragraph or a fenced code block read as a block of its own and a comment whose own block was deleted could still be moved onto it with nothing shown
proof.surface: Dispatch's web app in Chromium through Playwright, against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector, and the proof-editor unit suite
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait
proof.observed: 15 passed (10.3m). Edges are block offsets now, never a character: `readingsOf` takes the blocks it is scanning in place of `positionAt` and the `acrossBlocks` flag, so both character tests are gone - a remembered-whole prefix must start at a block's own `at`, a remembered-whole suffix must end at its `at + length`, found by the halving search `positionIn` already used, shared as `blockAt`. The reader's-block step and `placementOf` pass a one-element list; the document step passes `documentText`'s own blocks. The reviewers' reproduction is a compose-wait row: the reader selects a whole block whose words also read on a hard-break line of the next paragraph, the sweep takes the mark while the tab is away, that block loses the words, and Send refuses with the draft kept and nothing marked.
proof.negativeControl: Putting the character test back fails the new hard-break unit row with a fresh mark on the second paragraph's line and placement `prefix "Notes:\n", suffix "\nLater text here."` - the reviewers' reproduction exactly. Unit rows also cover a fenced code block's line and the document-wide two-readings case after a whole-block deletion, which nothing covered before.

proof.surface: The margin's and the document's own React tests
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test --parallel web/src e2e/__tests__
proof.observed: 2988 pass. The pending report is sent on both outcomes of a row's write, so a count skipped while a write was in flight is shown whether the store takes the row or refuses it, with a row driving a refused write while an earlier count is held. The composer keeps saying it is re-attaching until the retry answers, instead of falling back to the server's words in the middle of the wait, with a row that holds `whenSent` open across the assertions. The false 'and their words never moved' is deleted from the test whose paragraph is dropped.
proof.negativeControl: Each of the two behaviour fixes has a row that fails without it; the prose one is a deletion, checked by reading the row it sits on.

proof.criterion: Nothing else in the application broke, and the merge of main changed none of this branch's lines
proof.surface: The whole Chromium e2e project, and the fingerprint over the pull request's own diff
proof.observed: 941 passed, 0 failed (1.5h) at the merge head. main was merged for its CI fixes (#2601, the claim-list parser that follows #2598), with no conflict; the fingerprint over this pull request's own lines is c0867d151eb313a66e61e744b2b352eed1077d981bce473ab9e9d76b76819227 on both sides, unchanged. The 15 rows, both typechecks, both unit suites, biome, the README's line-break check, go vet, gofmt and the Go sweep tests (197s) were all run at that head.
proof.negativeControl: The fingerprint is computed from the fork point at each head, so a merge touching one of this branch's lines would change it; it did not.

filesChanged: packages/proof-editor/src/record-mark-retype.ts and tests/record-mark-retype.test.ts (blocks instead of newlines, three new rows, the prose deletion)
trickyParts: The document's one text is read with `textBetween(…, "\n", "\n")`, which turns a hard break into a newline and keeps a code block's own line breaks, so no character in that text tells a block separator from a line. Only the block offsets `documentText` already returns can, which is why every scan is now given them.
Passing the blocks instead of a position function also removed the two closures each scan allocated, and left one way to ask where a block begins and ends.
openQuestions: The reported 'about ten seconds' is still unexplained, as every round has recorded.
main's flaky listener test is #2594's, which had still not landed when this round merged main; #2598 and #2601, the deterministic ci-ok failures, are both in.
discoveredComplexity: The PR body's 'Re-measured as promised' line said the accepted sentence-rewrite limit was the only way a record could reach a passage the reader did not select. This round's finding made that false, and the line is corrected to say what the limit is and what closed the other way.
The simplify pass is spent (round 1, ce-simplify-code at 96a647eb, applied). A round answering a review runs none.
